caption:
The government might add $500 to your super. Most people who qualify never trigger it.

It's called the super co-contribution. Put your own after-tax money into super and the government can add up to 50c for every dollar, to a maximum of $500 a year. So $1,000 in can mean $500 added.

Who gets it (2026–27):
- Total income of $49,293 or less: the full amount.
- It fades out and stops at $64,293.
- At least 10% of your income comes from a job or business.
- Under 71, not on a temporary visa, and you lodge a tax return.

The catch: it only applies to contributions you don't claim as a tax deduction, and the money is locked in super until you retire.

There's no form. The ATO works it out when you lodge and pays it to your fund.

Know someone working part-time who should see this?

Narrated by an AI voice.
